summary.text: 二 is the numeral sign for two, drawn as two horizontal strokes. Its simple construction is best explained as an indicative counting sign; the historical account that it doubles 一 is compatible with this reading, though the dossier does not establish the graph’s original formation. [ref002, ref004, ref012, ref014]

formation.text: Indicative: two parallel strokes mark the quantity two. The Han-dynasty Shuowen account describes 二 as formed by paired ones, and later commentary explains this as doubling 一. This is a historical interpretation, not independent proof of the graph’s origin. [ref004, ref012]

components.text: The whole graph is the picture-like arrangement of two horizontal strokes used as a counting sign. It has no meaningful internal components; the Shuowen account of paired 一 describes how the strokes relate, not separate component roles. [ref002, ref012, ref014]

history.text: The selected historical glyph is a modern redraw of a form attributed to a mid-Western Zhou bronze context. It depicts two separate horizontal strokes. The dossier does not establish the earliest attested inscription or a detailed sequence of graphic changes. [ref026, ref032]

uncertainties.text: The Shuowen’s association with the number of earth and its paired-ones analysis are historical explanations, not proof of the graph’s first formation. The inspected evidence does not resolve the original account or establish the earliest attestation. [ref012, ref031, ref032]
The dossier documents numeral uses and later ordinal and figurative uses, but does not establish exact dates or a complete path between them. [ref015, ref023]

senses.text: The graph is used for the numeral two; the supplied quotations and summaries do not verify a dated earliest inscription or manuscript witness. [ref014, ref015]
A cited Tang poem uses 二 with ordinal meaning ‘second’; the exact development from the numeral sense is not established here. [ref015, ref023]

senses.gloss: divided or disloyal (as in 二心)
senses.text: A cited Zuo zhuan usage has 二心 meaning ‘divided’ or ‘disloyal heart’; its precise semantic path and earliest date are unresolved. [ref015, ref023]
‘Twice’ is recorded as a current gloss, but the dossier supplies no evidence establishing its chronology or development. [ref006]

limitations.text: Numeral, ordinal, figurative and ‘twice’ glosses do not by themselves establish chronology or semantic links; no development is asserted here. [ref006, ref015, ref023]

The dossier’s proposed sound reconstructions and cross-language comparisons concern the spoken numeral, not graphic formation; their comparative basis was not independently assessed. [ref016, ref018, ref024]

overview.text: 二 is the numeral two, represented by two horizontal strokes. The old explanation that it pairs or doubles 一 fits that construction, though it does not prove how the graph first arose. [ref002, ref012]

components.text: Read the graph as two strokes together: the complete sign represents the quantity two, rather than separate meaningful parts. [ref002, ref014]
